newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia wants Newmonth to cut gold stake.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia wants Newmonth to cut gold stake.

text.p: Indonesia has asked the U.S. Newmont Mining Corp to cut its 80-percent stake in the Batu Hijau goldfield to 49 percent, the director-general of mining, Adjat Sudradjat said on Friday.

He said Newmont should transfer its shares to Indonesian companies, adding that it had been agreed that Newmont would its stake in Batu Hijau to 49 percent between the fifth and 10th year of operations at the site.
Sudradjat said Newmont was granted a contract of work for the Batu Hijau project 11 years ago.
Bisnis Indonesi newspaper said commercial production at the field, which contained about 14.7 million ounces of gold, was due to start by 2000.

"The government has asked Newmont to reduce its stake in the Batu Hijau project," Sudradjat told reporters while accompanying Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana on the general election campaign trail in East Kalimantan province.
He said the situation in the local mining industry had changed over the years, with more local companies now capable of venturing into the sector.
"Many national mining companies now have the capability," he said. "Newmont should understand the current conditions."
